presentation.summary: Manage a deep excavation through an old utility corridor where buried electrical and gas services are uncertain and ground conditions deteriorate.
presentation.role: You are the safety professional responsible for an excavation beside buried electrical and gas services.
presentation.situation: A deep trench is planned through an old utility corridor. Drawings are incomplete, soil conditions are variable and the work can expose workers to service strikes, collapse and hazardous releases.
presentation.objective: Verify underground services, protect the excavation, stop when conditions differ from the plan and manage any release without creating secondary casualties.
knownFacts: The trench will exceed normal standing depth.
Utility drawings may not reflect actual service positions.
Gas and electrical services cross the work area.

excavation_permit.title: Excavation permit
excavation_permit.summary: Excavation permit defines the authorized scope, conditions, hold points and required controls for the work.
excavation_permit.details:
Check that the scope and location match the actual task.
Confirm required controls and hold points are satisfied.
Treat changed conditions as a trigger for reassessment.

utility_location_decision_best.observable: The team verifies the decisive safeguards at the locate buried services stage before exposure continues. The excavation moves forward from a controlled condition.
utility_location_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

utility_location_decision_defensible.observable: The action improves control at the locate buried services stage, but one important verification or scope gap remains. Work proceeds with less assurance.
utility_location_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This is professionally plausible and partly correct, but it leaves one material criterion unresolved compared with the BEST action.

utility_location_decision_weak.observable: Preparation or work continues while a significant control question remains unresolved at the locate buried services stage. The available recovery margin decreases.
utility_location_decision_weak.guidedInsight: The action contains a valid element, but sequencing is weak because work advances before the decisive safeguard has been verified.

utility_location_decision_critical.observable: The excavation proceeds on an unsupported assumption at the locate buried services stage. A critical safeguard is bypassed and risk escalates sharply.
utility_location_decision_critical.guidedInsight: A critical choice often sounds efficient because it relies on prior status, appearance or experience. High-hazard work requires positive verification of the critical barrier.

trench_protection_decision_defensible.observable: The action improves control at the select trench protection stage, but one important verification or scope gap remains. Work proceeds with less assurance.
trench_protection_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This is professionally plausible and partly correct, but it leaves one material criterion unresolved compared with the BEST action.

trench_protection_decision_weak.observable: Preparation or work continues while a significant control question remains unresolved at the select trench protection stage. The available recovery margin decreases.
trench_protection_decision_weak.guidedInsight: The action contains a valid element, but sequencing is weak because work advances before the decisive safeguard has been verified.

trench_protection_decision_best.observable: The team verifies the decisive safeguards at the select trench protection stage before exposure continues. The excavation moves forward from a controlled condition.
trench_protection_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

trench_protection_decision_critical.observable: The excavation proceeds on an unsupported assumption at the select trench protection stage. A critical safeguard is bypassed and risk escalates sharply.
trench_protection_decision_critical.guidedInsight: A critical choice often sounds efficient because it relies on prior status, appearance or experience. High-hazard work requires positive verification of the critical barrier.

service_change_decision_defensible.observable: The team pauses part of the activity and gathers more information, but some exposure or uncertainty remains during the respond to an unexpected service stage.
service_change_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This choice recognizes the change, yet it leaves a narrower safety margin than a full stop-and-reassess response.

service_change_decision_best.observable: The team stops or stabilizes the work when conditions change at the respond to an unexpected service stage. The new condition is verified before the task continues.
service_change_decision_best.guidedInsight: Changing conditions invalidate earlier assumptions. The BEST response creates a deliberate hold point and reassesses the controls before exposure continues.

service_change_decision_weak.observable: The work continues under modified monitoring or local precautions even though the respond to an unexpected service condition has changed materially. Risk begins to rise.
service_change_decision_weak.guidedInsight: Extra observation is not equivalent to restoring a failed or uncertain barrier. Changed conditions should be controlled, not merely watched.

service_change_decision_critical.observable: The changed condition is effectively accepted and the excavation continues. A critical barrier is lost and the scenario moves into emergency territory.
service_change_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Proceeding because an alarm limit, schedule or visible condition has not yet become extreme can miss the earlier point where safe intervention was still easy.

collapse_decision_defensible.observable: The immediate area is secured and help is mobilized, but one element of the control collapse and release signs response remains less complete than the preferred plan.
collapse_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This action can reduce harm, but the BEST response integrates personnel protection, alarm, isolation and planned emergency control without leaving a material response gap.

collapse_decision_weak.observable: Some protective action is taken, but personnel remain closer to the hazard than necessary during the control collapse and release signs response. The margin for a secondary casualty narrows.
collapse_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A partial emergency action may sound practical, but it is weak when it keeps people exposed or delays full hazard-zone control.

collapse_decision_critical.observable: An unprotected or inadequately controlled intervention is attempted during the control collapse and release signs stage. The event escalates and a secondary casualty or larger release becomes credible.
collapse_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Critical emergency decisions often fail by sending people toward an uncontrolled hazard. Protect responders and establish control before attempting intervention.

collapse_decision_best.observable: The team activates the planned emergency response at the control collapse and release signs stage, keeps people out of the hazard zone and controls the event before re-entry.
collapse_decision_best.guidedInsight: The strongest emergency choice protects responders first. Rescue, isolation and source control should follow the planned capability rather than expose another person.

closeout_decision_best.observable: The excavation remains suspended while causes, damaged safeguards and corrective actions are verified. Work is reauthorized only after a safe basis is re-established.
closeout_decision_best.guidedInsight: Safe closeout is not simply returning conditions to normal. It must address why control was lost and verify the barriers needed for a safe restart.

closeout_decision_defensible.observable: The team strengthens the immediate controls and uses a controlled restart review, but the closeout does not explore the underlying failure as completely as the BEST path.
closeout_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: Corrective action is valuable, but restart assurance is stronger when the underlying cause and all affected safeguards are verified.

closeout_decision_weak.observable: The team corrects the most visible problem and prepares to resume the excavation before the full causal chain has been resolved.
closeout_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A technically acceptable local fix can still be weak if it restores production before learning and system-level corrections are complete.

closeout_decision_critical.observable: The excavation is pushed toward restart after only superficial recovery. Critical causes or damaged safeguards remain unresolved.
closeout_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Restart pressure can recreate the same hazard. A major event is more likely when work resumes before critical barriers are restored and verified.

safe_completion.title: Safe completion
safe_completion.narrative: The excavation was completed with the critical hazards controlled and changing conditions managed before escalation.
safe_completion.keyTurningPoint: You verified the utilities and ground controls before exposing workers to the trench.

controlled_recovery.title: Controlled recovery
controlled_recovery.narrative: The excavation developed a significant control weakness, but later decisions restored a controlled state before serious harm occurred.
controlled_recovery.keyTurningPoint: A discrepancy was found, but the work was stopped and brought back under controlled conditions.

incident_contained.title: Incident contained
incident_contained.narrative: The scenario developed into an incident, but emergency and recovery actions contained the event and limited its consequences.
incident_contained.keyTurningPoint: Ground or utility conditions deteriorated, but evacuation and emergency controls limited the event.

major_incident.title: Major incident
major_incident.narrative: Unresolved control failures allowed the excavation to escalate into a major incident requiring extended response, investigation and corrective action.
major_incident.keyTurningPoint: Unresolved service and ground risks combined into a major excavation incident.

critical_failure.title: Critical failure
critical_failure.narrative: The decision path produced a severe uncontrolled outcome in the excavation. Recovery options were overwhelmed by a critical barrier failure.
critical_failure.keyTurningPoint: A decisive excavation or utility safeguard was bypassed while workers remained exposed.
